column7: admin restore was index-blind to WHEN a backup was taken relative to subsequent legitimate changes: restoring an archive older than what this host had already certified silently resurrected any access revoked since (a suspended account, a deleted machine credential, a rotated role grant) -- the restored database simply does not know the revocation happened, and verify-audit correctly reports the restored (shorter, self-consistent) chain as VALID either way, since a bare hash-chain re-walk cannot distinguish "shorter but genuinely older" from "truncated." design-b3-backup-v2.md section 6.3 implements the fix: admin backup records the source install's own signed audit high-water mark (system_metadata audit_checkpoint_highwater) in MANIFEST.json; every server mirrors that same mark to a host-local witness file (.audit-highwater-witness, sibling to the database, internal/core advanceAuditHighWater) as it advances; admin restore compares the archive value against the witness value BEFORE writing anything to disk and refuses if the archive is behind, requiring an explicit --allow-rollback (which itself writes an audit event recording the override) to proceed. Red-before/green-after: TestAdminRestore_RefusesRollback_WithoutOverride reproduces the exact repro (an older backup restoring silently, verify-audit reporting VALID) when the check is disabled, and refuses it with the fix in place.
